discovery: Prediction and discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: 2D materials and unconventional superconductivity
motivation: Bistritzer and MacDonald (PNAS 2011) predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become almost flat, so that interactions dominate the kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realised this experimentally, using a controlled tear-and-stack technique to produce magic-angle devices and discovering correlated insulating states and gate-tunable superconductivity. This was a simple, bold experiment: one material, carbon, and one new knob, the twist angle, produced a phase diagram resembling that of the cuprates, but controllable with a gate voltage in a single device. It started the field of 'twistronics' and moire quantum matter, which now includes correlated magnetism, orbital ferromagnetism, and the fractional quantum anomalous Hall effect. Laboratories around the world have reproduced and extended the work. It turned van der Waals heterostructures into a tunable platform for studying strongly correlated electrons.
